Industrial $423 million, up 1% sequentially and 4% year over year (energy infrastructure, medical and factory automation, partly offset by declines in the traditional industrial market). Other $400 million, up 34% sequentially, anchored by stronger than expected AI data center demand plus other end markets — 'The AI data center was the primary driver, but the other markets were also up, it wasn't 100% AI data centers.' Power Solutions Group (PSG) $829 million (+13% QoQ, +19% YoY); Analog and Mixed-Signal Group (AMG) $546 million (+1% QoQ, -2% YoY); Intelligent Sensing Group (ISG) $229 million (-3% QoQ, +7% YoY).

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and manufacturing, CEO Hassane El-Khoury: 'everything is constrained, whether it's internal or external, when it comes to short lead time'; onsemi believes it has good external capacity and allocation — 'We're not fighting for a lot of the advanced nodes on the compute side' — and services a lot of demand from die bank; the short-term issue is how quickly demand came in, not maximum capacity. 'We still do over 60% on internal manufacturing at onsemi, even with the divestitures.' 'We're not capped out. It's just how quickly we get there.' Treo's capacity investment is done in East Fishkill, which 'is not fully utilized, so we have the runway to ramp'. In power, constraints exist in some lanes from high voltage to low voltage; onsemi is running its most efficient power product 'in multiple fabs now' and increasing capacity and flexibility. CFO Thad Trent: 'Not all capacity is fungible ... We do have some supply constraints on certain lanes'; about 12% of capacity was taken offline, depreciation is now steady state, and capex is maintenance (multi-year target in the mid-single-digit percentage range). On input costs the CEO said many supplier increases take effect in Q4 and, for 2027, 'we're not going to have any reductions or annual reductions'.
quarterly_data.figure: over 60% internal manufacturing; ~12% of capacity taken offline

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Great Wall: CEO Hassane El-Khoury said onsemi 'secured two power supply platform wins with Great Wall, a leading provider of power solutions for China's cloud and AI infrastructure market'; AI data center revenue is 'primarily in the U.S.', with some China business with Great Wall 'starting for us as well'.

Automotive and Treo, CEO Hassane El-Khoury: in China, automotive content per vehicle is expanding with customers like Geely, Zeekr and Xiaomi; in the U.S. onsemi continues to gain share across EV disruptors (Rivian R2: MOSFETs in the zonal controller architecture, SiC in the onboard charging system); onsemi has won designs on hybrids in both China and North America, where hybrids were expected to stay on silicon or IGBT. 'We still believe we're shipping to true demand now. The inventory is behind us'; automotive demand is 'very stable with a good outlook'; order trends rank China, then the U.S., then Europe in both automotive and industrial. A growing share of recent design wins comes from products introduced over the last two years, including 10BASE-T1S Ethernet and inductive and ultrasonic sensing, reflecting Treo, the analog mixed-signal platform; Treo is starting to ramp in some zonal architectures, and onsemi remains 'on track to double the number of products sampling this year'. Over a multi-year period the CEO expects to outgrow underlying vehicle production.
quarterly_data.figure: Treo: on track to double products sampling in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Synaptics acquisition, CEO Hassane El-Khoury: Synaptics' connected compute capabilities complement onsemi's power, sensing and control 'at accretive gross margins', and the combination would use onsemi's manufacturing scale, global sales channel and mass market engine; 'We expect the transaction to close in mid-2027, subject to customary approvals.'

AI data center positioning, CEO Hassane El-Khoury: onsemi calls itself 'the only broad-based US power semiconductor supplier with technologies spanning the full AI power tree' (company claim), supporting the move to 800 V DC distribution 'from the grid all the way to the processor'; its high-voltage revenue is expected to accelerate as power requirements rise. In data center onsemi spans SiC MOSFETs, SiC JFETs and silicon at high voltage 'all the way to ... the SPS, which is right at the XPU'; 'The growth that we are seeing in AI data center is not necessarily anchored on the high voltage. We are gaining share and ramping close to the core as well'; wins announced over the last couple of quarters 'are now starting to ramp and contribute to revenue', and SiC growth is now visible in North America in PSUs. On the earlier AI data center outlook, 'We're not breaking it out beyond that at this point'; 'It is sustained strength. It's not a quarterly strength', and the 800 volt DC transition 'is going to fuel more of our content'.
